prov.text: Provision for Credit Losses. Based on management’s analysis of the adequacy of the ACL, a provision of $1.2 million was recorded for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, of which $1.4 million related to the provision for credit losses on loans, compared to a provision of $1.4 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, which included a $1.0 million provision for credit losses on loans. The increase in the provision for credit losses on loans was primarily driven by loan growth, charge-off replenishment and lower prepayment speed forecasts updated with rising interest rates. The provision for credit losses on unfunded commitments decreased $500,000 during the three months ended September 30, 2026 as a result of commercial and industrial drawdowns and credit line reductions.

nonint.text: Noninterest Expense. Noninterest expense increased $15.8 million, or 51.7%, to $46.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 from $30.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Salaries and employee benefit expenses increased $8.9 million, or 47.5%, resulting primarily from a $4.8 million increase in employee compensation, a $980,000 increase in medical and dental benefits, a $964,000 increase in employee bonus expense, a $335,000 increase in federal employer taxes and a $308,000 increase in 401(k) match expenses, all due to headcount increases related to the Provident acquisition and the Company’s continued organic growth; a $739,000 increase in pension expense resulting from a liquidation refund for the same amount during the quarter ended September 30, 2025; and a $434,000 increase in stock-based compensation as a result of the grants made during the current year. Data processing expenses increased $2.4 million, or 83.8%, primarily driven by our continued investment in technology and related systems in support of upcoming revenue initiatives, requiring the operation of systems in parallel for a period of time while new systems are implemented. Occupancy and equipment expenses increased $1.5 million, or 95.4%, primarily driven by the Provident acquisition, as well as the opening of three new branches and contract settlement fees.

nonop.text: Interest Expense. Total interest expense increased $11.2 million, or 33.4%, to $44.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 from $33.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Interest expense on deposits increased $11.6 million, or 37.2%, to $42.9 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 from $31.3 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase in interest expense on deposits was primarily driven by an increase in the average balance of certificates of deposit and individual retirement accounts of $749.2 million, or 38.7%, to $2.68 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 from $1.93 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2025; an increase in the average balance of money market accounts of $616.3 million, or 55.1%, to $1.74 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 from $1.12 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2025; and an increase in the average balance of NOW accounts of $302.6 million, or 64.7%, to $770.4 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 from $467.8 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, partially offset by a decrease in the weighted average rate on certificates of deposit and individual retirement accounts of 28 basis points to 3.89% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 from 4.18% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.

net.text: Net Income. Net income increased $7.8 million, or 50.6%, to $23.1 million, or $0.58 per diluted common share, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income of $15.4 million, or $0.43 per diluted common share, for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Net interest income increased $23.3 million, or 48.3%, and noninterest income increased $1.4 million, or 38.6%, partially offset by increased noninterest expense of $15.8 million, or 51.7%, and increased income tax expense of $1.3 million, or 27.9%.

ocf.text: Our cash flows are comprised of three primary classifications: cash flows from operating activities, investing activities, and financing activities.

Net interest income.text: Net Interest Income. Net interest income increased $23.3 million, or 48.3%, to $71.4 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 from $48.2 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to a $2.09 billion, or 41.2%, increase in the average balance of interest-earning assets to $7.15 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 from $5.06 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 and a decrease in the weighted average rate on interest-bearing liabilities of 28 basis points to 3.18% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 from 3.46% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. These increases were partially offset by an increase in the average balance of interest-bearing liabilities of $1.74 billion, or 45.4%, to $5.59 billion at September 30, 2026 from $3.84 billion at September 30, 2025.

Noninterest income.text: Noninterest Income. Noninterest income increased $1.4 million, or 38.6%, to $5.1 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 from $3.7 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The increase resulted primarily from increased customer service fees of $1.0 million, or 40.3%, due to higher cash management, loan and debit card fees.
